craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as difference uncut; vyabhicāri clarity (prasāda) of the mirror-list (C1 rasa block). Sanskrit-first: na…vicchinna (NOT cut off — the negation governs both splits); svacchāt…ekadhāmnaḥ (from the free, the clear, the one-abode — triple ground-name); maṇidarpaṇādike (jewel-mirror-ETC — ādi closes). Rows: 9 (bare list palace→mountain + jewel/mirror — the list IS the proof, kept bare), 10 (jewel-mirror left standing, no gloss), 1 (‘abode’ gathers L1; L2 closes on ‘and the like’ — ādi enacted: the catalogue refusing to close IS the doctrine). Close: ‘and the like’. Rupture: colon after ‘from it’ (ground stated, then its triple name). Rejected: trimming to three items — killed: six named + ‘rest’ is the pervasion proved; closing on ‘mirror’ — killed: Sanskrit ends ādike, openness load-bearing. Read aloud: THAT-split — AND-this-ONE — is NOT cut-OFF … PA-lace, E-le-phant, HORSE, CLOUD, O-cean, MOUN-tain … JUST-as with JEW-el, MIR-ror, AND-the-LIKE.

lines: That split — and this one — is not cut off from it: from the free, the flawlessly clear, the single abode.
Palace, elephant, horse, cloud, ocean, mountain, and the rest — just as with jewel, mirror, and the like.

reads_against.argmap: Difference is not cut off from its ground — free, most-clear, one-abode — then the bare list against the jewel-mirror: palace through mountain, just as from jewel-mirror and the like. → Difference uncut from its ground; the bare list its proof.
